title: Madhya Pradesh High Court Holds 24-Year-Old Arbitral Award Execution Time-Barred
case_name: Ashok Kumar v. Bhupendra Kumar Lunkad
card_summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court at Indore held a 2024 execution petition on a 2000 arbitral award was time barred. The award became enforceable in January 2002, when Section 34 objections to it were dismissed, so the twelve-year period under Article 136 expired in January 2014. The court rejected the plea that limitation should run from a later 2019 order, holding an award does not merge into a Section 34 or 37 order.
card_tip: Count the twelve-year limitation clock for executing an award from the date Section 34 objections are dismissed, not from a later appellate order, and file execution well inside that window.
verification_notes: Corroborated by Verdictum (order PDF watermarked 23-10-2026, Justice Vinay Saraf, Indore Bench), LiveLaw Biz and Free Press Journal, all reporting the same Civil Revision No. 1152 of 2026 and the same holding on merger and limitation. Background facts (1989 suit, 2000 award, 2002 Section 34 dismissal, 2019 High Court order, 2024 execution petition) are consistent across all three reports.
